messages:
Maya R: Customer reports intermittent 5xxs from hosted inference since ~08:12 PDT. Large customer 'AcmeDocs' sees generation requests fail and still get billed. They provided a few correlation IDs. Anyone seeing platform-side spike?

Sam (oncall): Yep seeing a spike in 502/503s around 08:10-08:30. Quick curl repro from their trace id:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"upstream_error", "message":"gateway: control-plane dependency failed"}
```
Logs from gateway show repeated lines: `control-gw: upstream auth/session timeout (504)`, `routing-policy: 503 Service Unavailable`, and fast-fail pathing. Sample from svc logs: 
```
[08:12:14] authz-svc warn: upstream call to session-store timed out after 1200ms (attempt=1) trace=tr_0a1b2c
[08:12:14] routing-policy error: failed to resolve route for key tenant=acmedocs err=configdb: read timeout
[08:12:14] gateway error: upstream returned 502 (authz->routing-policy)
```
Alex P: I pulled metrics — routing-policy p99 latency jumped and config-db read latencies show timeouts. There was a config push at 07:58 that changed a routing policy cache TTL and a circuit-breaker threshold (PR #4127). Hypothesis: new config caused cache miss storm hitting config DB and exhausting read connections, causing auth/session lookups to cascade into 5xx.

Luis - Support: Customer says they were charged for the failed requests. We should coordinate billing credit and inform them of mitigation steps. Please capture exact request ids to refund.

infra-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0257, paging eng-infra and eng-runtime.

Maya R: Immediate action: rollback the routing-policy config from PR #4127 and scale config-db read replicas by +1. Sam, please run rollback and confirm. Also throttle consumer traffic if necessary.

Sam (oncall): Rolling back now (08:34). Commands I ran:
```
# rollback applied config via console api
redwoodctl config rollback --service routing-policy --rev 4127
# scale read replicas (postgres read pool)
pgctl scale --cluster configdb --replicas 3
```
Rollback applied at 08:35. Error rate dropped to baseline within ~90s. Post-rollback logs show normal auth/session hits and routing-policy cache hits recovering.

Alex P: Repro steps for validation (do not run against prod traffic except with test keys):
1) With a test tenant, remove routing-policy cache to force configdb reads.
2) Fire a small burst of generation requests that need route resolution.
3) Watch configdb read_latency and connection_pool_exhaustion metric.
4) Observe gateway 502s when pool exhausted.

Luis - Support: Noted. I'll open a refund request for AcmeDocs with the list of failed correlation ids and propose a pro-rated credit for the time window 08:10-08:36. Will follow up with the account.

Sam (oncall): Monitoring shows stable now. Will keep incident open until EOD and run a capacity test on config-db in staging with the config change. Next steps: revert change, add a gradual ramp for TTL changes, add circuit-breaker fallback to cached default routing, and increase configdb connection_pool.

Maya R: Thanks. Please add a short postmortem in incidents/ after the incident: include root cause (config change causing cache miss storm -> configdb pool exhaustion -> auth/session/routing 5xx), mitigation steps we took, and a permanent fix plan. Also add a KB entry for support on how to respond to billed-but-failed cases and the refund workflow.

Sam (oncall): Will do. Updating INC-2026-0257 with timeline, rollback timestamp, and candidate fixes.

infra-bot: Alert cleared at 08:38.

Maya R: Marking this as high-priority follow-up. Assigning to Alex and infra for replay in staging and to create a safe rollout checklist for routing-policy changes.

Alex P: I'll draft the checklist and a small load test to validate configdb connection headroom.

Luis - Support: I'll keep AcmeDocs updated; will escalate billing if they push.

(END)
